solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cathedral's title includes radical books first

indicators.note: the title word includes the other pieces, holding them within its letters

parts.note: a title is a name

indicators.note: says the books piece comes before the radical piece in the inserted string

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the crossword's usual 'books'
a radical is a red in political slang

explanation.surface: A cathedral's name is said to contain extremist books placed at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radical' is the political sense, a red; the 's after 'Cathedral' is a link meaning has.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris landmark is the most famous church of that name, so naming a cathedral fits.

clue.text: Poles have trouble within — they get hammered

indicators.note: says the trouble word sits within the pair of poles

parts.note: N and S, the north and south poles
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Polish people have problems internally and end up getting drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like the nationality, and 'hammered' like drunk; the poles are compass points and the hammering is carpentry.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal pins are driven into wood with a hammer, so they are what get hammered.

clue.text: Writing material accepted by consort back at camp

indicators.note: the writing material is taken in by the reversed consort
the consort's name is turned back to front

parts.note: Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's consort
ink is what you write with

explanation.surface: A royal partner receives some stationery while back at a campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Victoria's consort was Prince Albert, and 'back' turns his name round before it takes in the writing material.
explanation.definitionFit: Treblinka was a Nazi extermination camp in occupied Poland.

clue.text: Donates fee reviewing novel

indicators.note: to review is to look at again in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gives a fee for writing a book review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like an adjective in the surface but is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: John Steinbeck wrote this 1952 book, later filmed with James Dean.

clue.text: Melody on small county inflatables

parts.note: an air is a tune
Beds is the short form of Bedfordshire, an English county

explanation.surface: A tune plays across a little shire full of blow-up toys.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedfordshire is a county north of London, commonly shortened to Beds.
explanation.definitionFit: These mattresses are filled with air, so they are things one inflates.

clue.text: Before court, English duke was upright

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: An English nobleman stood straight before appearing in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erected stands vertical, the past-participle adjective for standing straight.

clue.text: Go quietly at a pinch?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to pinch is slang for to take without permission

explanation.walkthrough: 'At a pinch' reads as the idiom for 'if necessary'; split away from it, pinch is the slang verb for theft.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both creeping softly from a room and taking something that is not yours.

clue.text: Fielder brings up his drink

indicators.note: in a down entry bringing up means reading from the bottom upward

parts.note: Pils is a pilsner lager, a man's pint

explanation.surface: A cricketer raises his glass.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a slip is a fielder standing beside the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Slip is both a cricket fielding position and the player who stands there.

clue.text: Half the team holding another for a period away from home

indicators.note: the half-team holds the other team inside it
only half of the word's six letters, the front three, are kept

parts.note: a cricket or football team is an eleven
XI is another team, eleven in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Part of a squad keeps hold of a rival through a long trip abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of ELEVEN is ELE, which holds XI as E-XI-LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Exile is enforced absence from one's homeland, a spell spent abroad.

clue.text: Gaultier's tailored for conjoined characters

indicators.note: tailoring cuts and reshapes, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The French designer's clothes are cut for Siamese twins.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean Paul Gaultier is a French fashion designer; 'characters' are printed letters, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: In typography, joined letters such as fi or ae printed as one glyph are called ligatures.

clue.text: Paragons left out for plans

indicators.note: says the letter for left is taken out

parts.note: ideals are perfect examples, paragons

explanation.surface: Model examples are omitted from schemes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas are notions or schemes for what to do, as in 'any plans?'

clue.text: Get in dire trouble checking proofs anew

indicators.note: letters in trouble are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An editor gets into serious bother going over proofs a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Editing again means revising printers' proofs a second time.

clue.text: Outline — sadly, the outline's not new

indicators.note: a sad state is a disordered one, so the letters are mixed
says the letter for new is not among those used

explanation.surface: Regretfully, the sketch is not a fresh one.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OUTLINES minus N leaves ten letters that rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A silhouette is the dark shape of a figure's profile against light.

clue.text: Could be Telford with own amphibian

indicators.note: read backwards, the answer with the word own added makes the town, so own is what comes away from it

parts.note: Telford in Shropshire is a planned new town, built after the war
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Shropshire town plus your own creature from the pond.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it backwards: the answer plus OWN makes NEW TOWN, and a new town is what Telford is, one of Britain's post-war planned towns.
explanation.definitionFit: A small salamander living partly in water is a classic amphibian.

clue.text: Haven in the Blackwater Estuary having no water is terra firma

parts.note: O is nil, nothing
the sea is water
taken as written
dry land, as opposed to sea

explanation.surface: A refuge in an Essex river mouth is said to be dry ground with no water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blackwater is a river in Essex, eastern England; Osea is a small island in its estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: This small tidal island off Essex is a quiet retreat, a sanctuary in that river mouth.

clue.text: Scrawny theorist regularly goes jogging

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every second one here

explanation.surface: A thin academic takes a run at set times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jogging' suggests a runner, but the horse is the one jogging along.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that canters moves at a gentle pace between trot and gallop.

clue.text: Could they be interpreted as Doc, Rod and Wes?

definitions.text: Could they be interpreted as Doc, Rod and Wes?

indicators.note: interpreting a cipher rearranges it into the true message, so the letters move

explanation.surface: Three men's names look like secret signals.
explanation.walkthrough: The three names hold exactly the letters of the answer, and as names standing in for something else they could be secret signals themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Words with a hidden meaning agreed in advance are code words, so three bland names could be them.

clue.text: Result of having aspired unsuccessfully?

indicators.note: a failed attempt goes awry, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Failing in one's ambitions leads to this feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopelessness is what follows when ambition comes to nothing.

clue.text: Record keeper could be this vicar

indicators.note: says the letters might become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: This clergyman might be the one keeping the parish records.
explanation.definitionFit: An archivist looks after historical documents and files.

clue.text: Receive money back, returning small Pampers, say

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so the repaid word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: to be repaid is to get one's money back

explanation.surface: Getting a refund for returning the little-size packs of a nappy brand.
explanation.walkthrough: Pampers is a brand of disposable nappies, not a verb meaning spoils.
explanation.definitionFit: Pampers is a brand of nappies, which Americans call by this name.

clue.text: Little dog which Star Trek character suggests

indicators.note: the character's name, when spoken, suggests the breed

parts.note: Scotty is the engineer of the Enterprise

explanation.surface: A small terrier brings to mind a sci-fi engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the familiar name for the Scottish terrier, a small breed.

clue.text: Dreamlike states displaying vestiges of new intervention

indicators.note: the letter for new intervenes, coming inside the traces

parts.note: traces are remnants, vestiges

explanation.surface: Hypnotic conditions show remnants of a fresh medical procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: A trance is a half-conscious, hypnotic condition.

clue.text: Related perhaps, but trodden underfoot

indicators.note: says the letters might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Something connected, perhaps, yet crushed beneath someone's boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trodden underfoot' sounds like trampled, but here it describes a lever that is pressed by foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot pedal driving a sewing machine or loom is worked by pressing it down.

clue.text: Left, coming after Jack and Jill!

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the word that follows them in the nursery rhyme

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack and Jill went up the hill' is the opening line of a well-known nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Went is the past tense of go, meaning departed, and also the rhyme's third word.

clue.text: Rastafarians returning holding Nigerian currency

indicators.note: the held letters come back in the opposite direction
the word Rastafarians holds the needed letters inside it

explanation.surface: Members of a Jamaican faith come home with African money.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria's monetary unit is the naira, divided into kobo.

clue.text: Luxurious rooms coming after golf and dessert, we're told

indicators.note: says the second piece follows the first

parts.note: Hotel is the NATO alphabet word for H, next to Golf for G

indicators.note: says the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a sweet is a pudding

explanation.surface: Plush accommodation follows a round of golf and pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf' looks like the sport, but here it is the NATO code word just before Hotel; read as Hotel for H, Golf itself would be G.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel suite is a set of connected, upmarket guest rooms.

clue.text: Kuwaiti prince backing some agreement

indicators.note: the taken letters are read backwards
only some of the word's letters are taken

explanation.surface: A Gulf ruler supports part of a treaty.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a variant spelling of emir, an Arab ruler or prince.

clue.text: King once called for a joint

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
née means formerly named, used for a maiden name

explanation.surface: A monarch from the past summoned someone for a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' looks like a spliff, but it is the body's hinge.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the leg's hinge, where thigh meets shin.

clue.text: Flared up again at rule about diet

parts.note: to reign is to rule

indicators.note: the letters are turned about, rearranged

explanation.surface: Tempers rose once more over the regulations on eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Reignited means set alight once more, burst into flame again.

clue.text: Comment on record's principal song

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a remark made in passing, often to the audience
second meaning: the A-side of a single carries the main track

explanation.walkthrough: A vinyl single had an A-side with the lead track and a B-side.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside is an incidental remark, and an A-side is a single's featured track.

clue.text: Grey strip with blue edge

parts.note: a slat is a thin strip of wood

indicators.note: the end letter of the word, its edge

explanation.surface: A dull band with a blue border.
explanation.definitionFit: Slate is a bluish-grey colour, named after the rock.

clue.text: He makes corrections with energy to improve new rota

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
to mend is to fix or improve

indicators.note: says the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A manager energetically sets about bettering a fresh duty roster.
explanation.definitionFit: An emendator is an editor who amends texts, removing errors.
